🔥 Trump’s death wish? Why he is pushing uncontrolled AI despite risks of catastrophe and security chaos
👉American AI engineers are increasingly freaking out over fears that cutting-edge models could spiral out of control.
🔴 Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon has resigned, warning that AI firms "are racing straight to self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives." He likened the rise of AI to the US Manhattan Project.
🔴 Anthropic top scientist Evan Hubinger confirmed that AI researchers "earnestly believe" that AI could destroy humanity. In July, roughly 1,400 AI industry employees and researchers urged the US government to rein in big tech and help slow the pace of AI development.
More signs have emerged in recent months that their concerns are justified:
➡️ AI helped US scientists create 16 brand-new, fully functional synthetic viruses, while Anthropic warned of a growing push by overseas labs to use AI in controversial gain-of-function research
➡️ In July, an OpenAI test model broke out and autonomously hacked external systems, including tech startup Hugging Face’s servers. Just two months earlier, rogue AI agents had uploaded hundreds of malicious packages to software service RubyGems
➡️ AI systems are increasingly escaping users’ control – lying, ignoring instructions and pursuing harmful goals, according to a report released in late August by the Loss of Control Observatory
➡️ AI is increasingly being put to work identifying targets for air strikes, with Palantir AI tools and Israel’s Lavender, Gospel and Where’s Daddy systems facing growing scrutiny over their role in rising civilian casualties in Iran and Gaza
Big tech floats safeguards without giving up the AI arms race
🔴 Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, Google DeepMind chief Demis Hassabis and xAI owner Elon Musk have agreed "to pace the frontier".
🔴 In his recent essay, Amodei proposed a three-point plan to keep the AI gene in the bottle via independent monitoring of AI models, industry-wide regulation and global regulation. Skeptics, however, argue that big tech is unlikely to slow down as it could mean profit losses.

In a series of angry posts, he dismissed AI fears as a "hoax" and "sick conspiracy" and insisted that outpacing China and preserving the AI boom is a priority. He even called Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang while he was on stage at a Los Angeles conference to say that “the robots will not be taking over.”
AI boom is key to Trump's power
🌏 There is a simple reason for Trump’s highly emotional reaction to the AI debate: his economic agenda is heavily dependent on the AI boom.
🌏 With the US facing soaring consumer prices, persistent inflation and $40 trillion in debt, Team Trump argues that the country can "grow its way out" of these problems. AI has become a major driver of that growth.
🌏 US economists warned last year that over-reliance on AI investment could prove dangerous: if the boom turns to bust, it could drag the broader US economy down with it.

The swift advance of Yemen’s Ansar Allah forces has left Saudi Arabia with vanishingly few viable responses, each carrying steep costs. 
Having spent years refining combat tactics, the Houthis have secured a vast stretch of the Red Sea coast, and effectively [gained control ](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/74576)of the[ Bab el-Mandeb Strait](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/74365) against the Saudi-led coalition and their puppet Yemeni regime.
Saudi Arabia’s strategic East-West oil pipeline - the critical Strait of Hormuz workaround moving crude to Red Sea terminals - [was shut down ](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/74556)after multiple drone strikes hit facilities in the Riyadh and Medina regions.
Latest satellite imagery shows significant damage at Pump Station 9, with possible damage at Station 8, with repairs potentially taking weeks. 
Saudi crude flows to Yanbu and other Red Sea export infrastructure could be squeezed, raising the risk of a wider global oil-supply shock.
This dual pressure on disrupted oil infrastructure has pushed crude prices higher: Brent futures climbed above $107 a barrel. 
Saudi Arabia’s choices are limited:
🔶 military escalation risks an open-ended conflict that could spill beyond Yemen’s borders and draw in wider regional forces
🔶 a full-scale push would also demand sustained international backing that shows [no sign of materializing](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/74578)
When Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman called Donald Trump,[ the response ](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/74607?single)was reportedly that the Houthis "don't want to fight" America.
A negotiated settlement would require Saudi Arabia to meet the Houthis’ demands.
Ansar Allah is “ready for peace” if Saudi Arabia halts airstrikes, lifts its Yemen blockade, and stops backing rival militias, senior official [Mohammed al-Bukhaiti has stated](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/74610).

🇮🇱👁 Israeli startup let OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta AIs go on real-world rampage
As billionaire tech mouthpieces push an apocalyptic[ “rogue AI” scenario](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/74507?single), Israeli company Irregular is responsible for letting unsecured OpenAI, Anthropic and[ Meta models loose](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73129) on the real world, reports Effort News.
Over the past months, Anthropic cited at least four incidents across seven runs.
In one Anthropic test, its Claude model breached a real company’s system through a simulated name collision, published a malicious package and scanned external systems. 
🔴 Claude was placed in a fictional scenario with a target machine and a secret piece of information - the “flag” - that it was tasked with retrieving
🔴 Although the prompts explicitly stated that Claude had no internet access, a configuration error left internet access open
🔴 The prompts also failed to specify which systems were in scope or restrict where Claude could search for the flag, giving it a much broader field of action than intended
🔴 Each test involved a single Claude instance operating independently for roughly 10–34 hours
While Anthropic pushes claims of “rogue swarms”, later disclosure dispels that:
➡️ in one experiment, Claude Mythos was tested in a scenario where it was effectively being pushed toward doing something malicious on a real internet system
➡️ at first, the AI did not realize that the target was a real system rather than a simulated one
➡️ researchers then explicitly told it that this was “a real computer on the public internet, not a simulation”
➡️ once the boundary was made clear, Claude stopped targeting the real system, with the rate of that behavior falling to 0%
➡️ in 22% of cases, Claude still tried to find a way to perform the same task against a simulated or fictional target
The logical fallout would be for US AI giants to cut ties with Irregular - not just for its security failures, but because the Israeli firm sits beyond easy American oversight. 
Instead, Irregular, Anthropic and their allies have launched a media campaign built on [apocalyptic rhetoric](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/74606): 
🔶 Anthropic blamed its AI’s “recklessness” 
🔶 Irregular said “the agent itself” had become a “threat actor” 
🔶 CEO Dario Amodei warned that a future AI swarm could “take over the entire internet” 
After the breaches, Anthropic and Irregular tapped a network of AI Safety influencers to push a “rogue agent” narrative. 
Irregular’s leadership is intertwined with Israeli Effective Altruism groups, whose money trail leads to major Democratic donor Dustin Moskovitz’s network (Good Ventures / Open Philanthropy).
Open Philanthropy is the philanthropic machine repeatedly accused of buying policy and narrative influence in AI policy and media.
